mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen from -23.4% (t-3w) to -19.1% (t-0w), a sustained 4.3-point recovery. This signals resumption of office commuting routines that directly increase weekday retail foot traffic, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.3 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 2 points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has declined from -34.4% (t-3w) to -29.1% (t-0w), indicating public transport avoidance persists. This suppresses retail access via mass transit, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains below -29% in all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -25% in week t+1 or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 points week-on-week in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized around -16% to -23% with no clear trend. When PARKS remains suppressed below -15%, outdoor recreation substitution is weak, forcing consumers toward indoor retail venues. This interaction between weak parks access and stable residential confinement (9.4-11.1%) drives RETAIL_REC upward as indoor alternatives become the primary outlet.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS averaged -17.7% over four weeks; RESIDENTIAL averaged 10.4%
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -10% in week t+1, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 8%, indicating reduced home confinement pressure.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable at -3.4% to -6.0%, indicating essential-goods access is maintained. When essential shopping is accessible and TRANSIT is severely constrained (below -30%), consumers consolidate trips to nearby retail clusters, increasing RETAIL_REC density in accessible zones over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30% AND GROCERY_PHARM remains within -3% to -6%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -29.1% in t-0w; GROCERY_PHARM at -5.1%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM volatility exceeds 2 points week-on-week, or TRANSIT rises above -25%, indicating policy relaxation that disperses trip consolidation.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September in Tokyo marks the end of summer heat and the approach of autumn shopping season. RETAIL_REC has shown marginal improvement from -26.9% (t-1w) to -23.7% (t-0w), a 3.2-point gain. Seasonal demand for fall merchandise will compound this trend, pushing RETAIL_REC further positive over the next four weeks independent of other mobility drivers.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.2 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines below -25% in week t+1, or external policy shock (e.g., new restrictions) is announced that overrides seasonal demand.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 11.1% (t-3w) to 9.4% (t-0w), indicating reduced home confinement. As people spend less time at home, they increase retail and recreation visits. This trend will accelerate RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks as residential baseline normalization continues.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.7 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 11% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite RESIDENTIAL decline, suggesting demand destruction rather than substitution.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are jointly suppressed (WORKPLACES -19.1%, TRANSIT -29.1%), indicating remote work and transit avoidance remain entrenched. When both remain below -18% and -28% respectively, the combined effect is a structural shift toward local, neighborhood retail rather than destination shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed relative to pre-pandemic baseline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -18% AND TRANSIT below -28% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both series remain suppressed in t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -15% or TRANSIT rises above -25% in week t+1, indicating structural shift toward office return and transit normalization.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has shown slight deterioration from -3.4% (t-2w) to -6.0% (t-1w) to -5.1% (t-0w), suggesting volatility in essential-goods access policy. When essential-goods mobility becomes unstable (variance > 1.5 points week-on-week), consumers delay discretionary retail trips and concentrate on essential shopping, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change exceeds 1.5 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM volatility from t-2w to t-0w is 2.6 points
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes within ±1 point of prior week, or RETAIL_REC increases despite GROCERY_PHARM volatility, indicating demand resilience.
